writer.headline: India’s voter-roll rules got tighter

tldr.text: India’s voter-roll tightening became clearer, with new declaration requirements and bigger deletions.
Karnataka’s final rolls shrank by nearly 1 crore after SIR deletions.
A Supreme Court fight is now over how strict registration can be.

intro.text: The biggest move was in India voter-roll tightening: the state’s registration process got more document-heavy, while deletions kept pulling rolls down. The Supreme Court is now part of the fight over SIR and Form 6.

threads.line: India’s voter-roll tightening advanced this week as the ECI added an extra declaration to Form 6, Karnataka’s final rolls shrank by nearly 1 crore after SIR deletions, and the Supreme Court became the venue for the dispute.

calls.note: No post-2026-10-27 official election commission or court filing in the week items clearly announced a new tighter voter-registration requirement.

writer.watch: Watch whether the Election Commission or courts turn the extra Form 6 declaration into a formal, durable rule. Also watch for fresh state-by-state roll revisions that show whether deletions are still spreading.
